questions.subject: PSYCHOLOGY
questions.topic: Personality: The Lexical Hypothesis
questions.stem: An engineer's brief asks which statement best captures the lexical hypothesis about personality traits.

options.text: Traits that matter most to a culture get encoded as single words in its language.
options.misconception: confuses lexical hypothesis with cultural priority

options.text: Personality can only be measured with single adjectives rather than sentences.
Important individual differences become represented as words in natural language.
Words for traits always map one-to-one onto biological mechanisms.

questions.explanation: The lexical hypothesis says salient individual differences get lexicalized. Option A narrows to culture, B to adjectives, D to biology, each overstating.
questions.hint: Think about why words exist for differences.

questions.stem: An engineer ranks six people twice and finds two swaps; what Spearman rho results if ranks are 1,2,3,4,5,6 then 1,2,4,3,5,6?
